# Discovery-prep brief: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Wyndham Hotels & Resorts is a public company (NYSE: WH) formed June 1, 2018 as a spin-off from Wyndham Worldwide, headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey. [4][5]
- Hotel counts vary by source: about 8,300 to 8,500 hotels across about 100 countries; the homepage says thousands of hotels in more than 95 countries. [1][2][3][5][6]
- It operates about 869,000 rooms, with 505,100 in the United States and 363,800 international at year-end 2025. [5][6][7]
- Its portfolio spans 25 brands including Super 8, Days Inn, Ramada, La Quinta, Wingate, Registry Collection and Wyndham, with midscale the largest segment (3,464 properties). [1][3][6][8]
- It reports more than 126 million enrolled loyalty members worldwide. [30]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- October 2026: Q3 2026 results raised the full-year 2026 outlook; global RevPAR grew 2% in constant currency versus Q3 2025. [9][10][11]
- July 2026: Q2 2026 results raised the full-year outlook; net income rose 17% year-over-year to $102 million. [9][10][11]
- September 2026: board approved a $400 million increase to the share repurchase authorization. [12][13]
- February 2026: announced intent to offer $650 million of Senior Notes due 2033. [9][10][11]
- May 2026: launched a native ChatGPT app; rooms bookable via Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, and Claude. [27]
- Development pipeline reached about 261,000 rooms as of June 30, 2026. [10]

## What guests say (themes)

- Cleanliness is the most-cited complaint in small review-site samples (grime, mildew, pests), though these samples mix in timeshare and rewards reviews. [15][16][17]
- Loyalty program account and points problems recur, including points not credited, locked accounts, and poor support response. [15][16][17][18]
- Front-desk service is mixed: some guests praise quick check-in and friendly staff, others report rude or unhelpful service. [15][16][17]
- Billing and value concerns recur, including unauthorized charges, delayed refunds, and account merge errors. [17][18]

## Technology hints

- Public materials name Aven Hospitality (formerly Sabre), Oracle, Amazon, Adobe and Salesforce as technology partners. [21]
- Wyndham Connect, powered by Canary Technologies, is used by nearly 2,000 North American hotels. [22]
- Wyndham Reservations Guest 360 is built on Salesforce Data 360, MuleSoft, Informatica and Agentforce Service. [25]
- No public reference was found to the booking engine or property management system vendor. [25]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which property management system and booking engine do franchised hotels run on today, and which are mandated versus optional?
2. How much of the reservations and call-center volume is handled by the Wyndham AI Concierge versus human agents, and where do calls still fall through?
3. What does the Wyndham Connect rollout look like for a franchisee: what does it cost, what is required, and how is adoption measured?
4. How are franchisees' data flows into Guest 360 handled, and which systems still hold their own copies of guest records?
5. Which loyalty account problems (points crediting, account locks, merges) generate the most support contacts, and how are they resolved today?
6. How are billing disputes and refunds processed across the franchise and corporate systems, and where do the errors start?
7. How are cleanliness and service scores tracked across franchised properties, and which signals reach the corporate team?
8. What is the process for a franchisee to request help or escalate an issue, and how long does it typically take?
9. Which parts of the 2026 rate and revenue management stack are centralized, and which do individual hotels control?
10. The public sources do not describe the pipeline of new openings or the Revo Hospitality rooms exclusion: how do those changes affect the systems and onboarding work your team would touch?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI reservations and call handling for franchised hotels | Autonomous call handling is already reported at more than 1,700 hotels, with a claimed handle-time reduction, so a focused tool for missed calls and after-hours booking may fit an existing push. [26][27] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Probably |
| Franchisee support and billing error triage | Billing errors, refund delays and account merge problems recur in reviews, and franchisees opt into tools like Wyndham Connect, so an owner-facing tool that flags and resolves billing errors could help. [17][18][28][29] | Probably | Unknown | No | Unknown |
| Loyalty account issue resolution | Points crediting and account lock complaints recur across review sources, and loyalty membership is large at over 126 million members, so faster resolution of these issues may matter. [15][16][17][18][30] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I am reaching out to ask for a 30-minute discovery call. I would like to learn how your reservations, franchise support and loyalty operations work day to day, and where the largest manual steps and recurring issues sit today. I am not coming with a product to pitch; I want to understand your current systems and priorities first.
>
> Would you have 30 minutes in the next two weeks? I can work around your schedule.
>
> Thank you,
> Vamsi

3. Is Harbor & Hearth the name of your hotel company, a restaurant or pop-up brand, or both?
4. How many rooms and food and beverage outlets do you run, and how are they split between owned and managed properties?
